Lectures 9 and 16 come after their peer feedback, so they are out of numerical order; the discussion of assignment 2 takes the first hour on 3 May. The new dates for lectures 7 and 13 follow.

```{=html}
<style>
/* The next lecture: KU red on the left, a light surface behind */
tr.next-lecture td { background: var(--surface) !important; font-weight: 400; }
tr.next-lecture td:first-child { box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 var(--accent2); }
/* Dates on one line */
main table td:nth-child(2) { white-space: nowrap; }
</style>
<script>
// Highlights the next lecture: the first row with a lecture number whose date
// is today or later. Dates are in 2027; rows without a date are skipped.
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
  const months = {Jan: 0, Feb: 1, Mar: 2, Apr: 3, May: 4, Jun: 5};
  const today = new Date();
  today.setHours(0, 0, 0, 0);
  for (const row of document.querySelectorAll('main table tbody tr')) {
    const cells = row.querySelectorAll('td');
    if (cells.length < 3 || !/^\d+\s/.test(cells[2].textContent.trim())) continue;
    const m = cells[1].textContent.match(/(\d{1,2})\s+(Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun)/);
    if (!m) continue;
    if (new Date(2027, months[m[2]], parseInt(m[1], 10)) >= today) {
      row.classList.add('next-lecture');
      break;
    }
  }
});
</script>
```
